text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- Stocks at Poland's private as well as small and big state-owned companies were to small in December to meet the market's demand for consumer goods, notably in the electronic, printing, leather and metal products' sectors, the Central Statistical Office (GUS) said. Public companies had excessive stocks of goods, it said.

- The first stage of the development of the planned Kedzierzyn-Kozle petrochemical complex, south-western Poland, will provide for building oil refining facilities within the next few years, a company leading the petrochemical consortium said after recent negotiations with the government.
- Poland's breweries sold 15.5 million hectolitres of beer in the first 11 months of 1996, a 9.4 percent increase compared with the same period last year, the Central Statistical Office (GUS) said.
- The Huta Ferrum steel mill will issue three million new shares in February, to raise funds for opeing a new pipe production line, the management said.
- The listed Echo Investment plans to sell its stake in the Projekt 55 Ltd to the Stinnes Market Budowlany for up to 16 million zlotys, Echo said.

- A regional electric power supplier in north-eastern Poland installed ultrasonorous devices on high voltage lines running through the Mazurian national park to frighten off birds of rare species inhabiting the area.

- Poland will not be allowed to enter the EU if it does not standardise weight and quality norms for foodstuffs, the state trading standards' authority (PIH) said. Over 35 percent of the examined pasta packs were underweight, PIH said.

- Only 13 local communes in the Przemysl province will be allowed to grow poppyseed next year following an intervention by the regional drug enforcement body. In the past the cultivation was allowed in 26 communes and the region was haunted by drug producers and dealers.
NOWA EUROPA
- Russia's fisheries' ministry is ready to allow Poland's deep sea fishermen a pollock quota of 120,000 tonnes while the fishermen demand a limit of 135,000 tonnes.

- The Sierakow Wielkopolski-based Warta SA glassworks have installed a new glass production facility, with a daily output of 250 tonnes, the Warta glassworks' marketing executive Danuta Wielinska said.

- Over 20,000 foreign hunters visit Poland every year, which earns the country up to 37 million marks, the Paged tours hunters' travel office said. Most of the hunters come from Germany, France, Italy, Austria and Denmark.
GAZETA WYBORCZA

- Poland's energy prices are expected to go up by more than 15 percent in January next year. The prices of fuels, public transport, postal and telecommunications service will also increase later in the first quarter, the finance ministry said.
- The listed Pekpol meat processor and trader plans a dynamic investment growth to devlop the Pekpol capital group's member companies, Pekpol said.
ZYCIE

- The listed Elektrim electrical engineering and foreign trade company has offered to build a bridge on the Vistula river in return for the ownership rights to the Praski river port in Warsaw, Elektrim said.
- Only a part of Poland's retailers will cut prices after the New Year to boost sales, the retailers said.
